question: I joined Larkmere 8 months before my baby is due and I'll be the primary caregiver. How much paid leave do I get, and can I split it into two parts?
documents:
Larkmere Analytics Ltd. - Parental Leave Policy (HR-POL-014, effective 1 March 2025)

1. Eligibility
Employees with at least 6 months of continuous service on the expected date of birth or adoption placement are eligible for paid parental leave. Employees with less than 6 months of service are entitled to unpaid parental leave only, up to a maximum of 12 weeks.

2. Paid leave entitlement
Primary caregivers: 16 weeks at 100% of base salary.
Secondary caregivers: 6 weeks at 100% of base salary.
Where both parents are employed by Larkmere, each parent receives their own entitlement. Entitlements cannot be transferred between parents.

3. Timing
Leave may begin no earlier than 4 weeks before the expected date of birth or placement and must be completed within 12 months of the birth or placement. Secondary caregiver leave may be taken in up to two blocks, each of at least 1 week. Primary caregiver leave must be taken as a single continuous block.

4. Notice
Employees must notify their manager and HR in writing at least 8 weeks before the intended start date. If the birth occurs early, notice should be given as soon as reasonably practicable.

5. Return to work
Employees returning from primary caregiver leave may request a phased return: 60% of normal hours at full pay for the first 4 weeks after returning. Phased return requests must be submitted at least 2 weeks before the end of leave.

6. Benefits during leave
Health, dental and life insurance coverage continue unchanged during paid leave. Pension contributions continue on the basis of full salary during paid leave. During unpaid leave, the employee must pay their share of health premiums to keep coverage active.

7. Related policies
For leave following pregnancy loss, see HR-POL-019 (Bereavement and Compassionate Leave).
response: You're eligible: 16 weeks at full base salary. It can't be split; only secondary caregiver leave can be taken in two blocks.

question: I've completed 4 years at Bramblecote and I'll have 12 unused PTO days at the end of this year. How many carry over, what happens to the rest, and by when do I need to use them?
documents:
Bramblecote Foods Inc. - Paid Time Off (PTO) Guidelines, 2026 edition

PTO combines vacation and personal days into one balance. PTO accrues each pay period (26 pay periods per year) based on completed years of service as of 1 January.

Completed years   Annual PTO   Accrual per pay period   Maximum carryover
0-2               15 days      0.58 days                5 days
3-5               20 days      0.77 days                8 days
6 or more         25 days      0.96 days                10 days

Carryover
At the end of the calendar year, unused PTO up to the maximum carryover for your tier is moved into the following year. Any unused PTO above the maximum is forfeited and is not paid out. Carried-over days must be used by 31 March of the following year; carried-over days not used by that date are forfeited.

Requests
PTO requests of 3 or more consecutive days require approval at least 2 weeks in advance. Requests of 1-2 days require 48 hours' notice. Managers may decline requests during the November-December peak production period at plants and distribution centres.

Negative balances
Employees may borrow up to 3 days of PTO they have not yet accrued, with manager approval. If employment ends with a negative balance, the borrowed amount is deducted from the final paycheck.

Termination
On leaving the company, accrued and unused PTO is paid out at the employee's base rate, except where employment is terminated for gross misconduct.

Questions about your balance should be directed to the People Services desk (ext. 4410).
response: 8 days carry over (the cap for the 3-5 year tier) and the other 4 are forfeited, not paid out. Use the 8 carried-over days by 31 March next year.

question: If I choose the Silver PPO with family coverage, how much will I pay in premiums over a full year, and do I get the company HSA contribution?
documents:
Corvane Logistics - 2026 Medical Plan Summary for Employees

Corvane offers three medical plans administered by Meridale Health Partners. All plans cover preventive care at 100% in-network.

Monthly employee contributions (deducted from pay)
Plan          Employee only   Employee + spouse   Family
Bronze HDHP   $42             $118                $176
Silver PPO    $96             $221                $318
Gold PPO      $154            $342                $489

Plan features (in-network)
Plan          Deductible (ind./family)   Coinsurance   Out-of-pocket max (ind./family)
Bronze HDHP   $3,200 / $6,400            20%           $6,500 / $13,000
Silver PPO    $1,500 / $3,000            20%           $5,000 / $10,000
Gold PPO      $500 / $1,000              10%           $3,000 / $6,000

Health Savings Account (HSA)
Employees enrolled in the Bronze HDHP receive an employer HSA contribution of $750 (employee only) or $1,500 (employee + spouse or family), deposited in two equal installments in January and July. Employees enrolled in the Silver PPO or Gold PPO are not eligible for an HSA but may use the Healthcare FSA (annual limit $3,300).

Enrollment
New hires must enroll within 30 days of their start date; coverage begins on the first day of the month following enrollment. Outside open enrollment (1-15 November), plan changes are allowed only after a qualifying life event, such as marriage or the birth of a child, reported within 31 days of the event.

Out-of-network care is covered by the Silver PPO and Gold PPO only, at 40% coinsurance after a separate deductible.
response: The Silver PPO family contribution is $318 per month, which comes to $3,816 over a full year. You wouldn't receive the employer HSA contribution, because that's only for Bronze HDHP enrollees; Silver PPO members can use the Healthcare FSA instead.

question: My grandmother passed away and the funeral is about 800 km from where I live. How many paid days off can I take?
documents:
Quillfield Mutual - Bereavement and Compassionate Leave (HR-POL-019)

Purpose
Quillfield Mutual recognises that employees may need time away from work following the death of a family member. This policy applies to all permanent and fixed-term employees from their first day of employment.

Paid bereavement leave
- Immediate family (spouse or partner, child, stepchild, parent, step-parent, sibling): up to 5 working days.
- Extended family (grandparent, grandchild, aunt, uncle, niece, nephew, parent-in-law, sibling-in-law): up to 2 working days.
- Pregnancy loss at any stage: up to 5 working days for either parent.

Travel allowance
Where the funeral or memorial service takes place more than 500 km from the employee's home, an additional 2 paid working days are granted for travel. This applies to both immediate and extended family.

Additional unpaid leave
With manager approval, employees may take up to 10 additional working days of unpaid leave, or use accrued annual leave, following any bereavement.

Timing
Bereavement leave does not need to be taken immediately but must be taken within 3 months of the death.

Documentation
Employees are not normally asked for documentation. HR may request reasonable evidence (such as a funeral notice) where an employee takes bereavement leave more than 3 times in a rolling 12-month period.

Pay
Paid bereavement leave is paid at the employee's normal base rate and does not include shift premiums or overtime.

Compassionate leave for serious illness of a family member is covered in HR-POL-020.
response: You can take up to 4 paid working days: 2 for the loss of a grandparent plus 2 travel days because the funeral is over 500 km away. The leave needs to be taken within 3 months of the death.

documents:

Annual limit

C                      75%
Below C / Fail         0%

question: My concert at Northgate was postponed and the new date was announced on 3 June. I can't make the new date. Until when can I request a refund, and will I get the service fees back?
documents:
Northgate Arena - Ticket Refund and Exchange Terms

These terms apply to all tickets purchased through the Northgate Arena box office or website.

1. Event cancellation
If an event is cancelled and not rescheduled, ticket holders automatically receive a full refund of the ticket price, service fees and delivery fees to the original payment method within 30 days of the cancellation announcement. No action is required.

2. Event postponement or rescheduling
If an event is postponed or rescheduled, tickets remain valid for the new date. Ticket holders who cannot attend the new date may request a refund of the ticket price within 14 calendar days after the new date is announced. Requests after this period will not be accepted. Service fees and delivery fees are refunded only when an event is cancelled.

3. Changes in venue or performer
A change in supporting act, seating configuration, or start time does not entitle ticket holders to a refund.

4. Buyer-initiated refunds
Tickets are otherwise non-refundable. Customers who purchased Ticket Protect (8% of the ticket price, added at checkout) may cancel for any reason up to 48 hours before the event start time and receive a refund of the ticket price. The Ticket Protect charge itself is not refundable.

5. Service fees
A service fee of $4.50 per ticket and an order delivery fee of $2.00 (mobile tickets free) apply to each order.

6. Resale
Tickets may be resold only through the Northgate Fan Exchange. Tickets resold elsewhere may be cancelled without refund.

How to request a refund: log in to your account, open the order, and select 'Request refund', or call the box office at 0300 555 0182 (10:00-18:00, Monday to Saturday).
response: Your deadline is 17 June, 14 calendar days after the new date was announced on 3 June. Only the ticket price is refundable for a postponement; service and delivery fees are refunded only for cancellations. You can request it from your account under 'Request refund' or by calling the box office.

question: I bought the Pinecrest annual plan for $144 on our website on 1 January and want to cancel on 20 April. How much will I get back?
documents:
Pinecrest Notes - Subscription, Cancellation and Refund Policy

Plans
Pinecrest Notes Pro is available as a monthly plan ($14 per month) or an annual plan ($144 per year, billed upfront; equivalent to $12 per month). Prices exclude applicable sales tax.

Cancelling a monthly plan
You can cancel a monthly plan at any time from Settings > Billing. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period, and you keep Pro access until then. We do not provide partial refunds for unused days of a monthly plan.

Cancelling an annual plan
- Within 14 days of the initial purchase or of an automatic renewal, you may cancel for a full refund.
- After 14 days, you may cancel and receive a prorated refund for each unused full calendar month remaining after the cancellation date, calculated at $12 per month, less a $15 early-termination fee.
- Your Pro access ends on the date of cancellation for annual plans refunded under this section.

Renewals
Annual plans renew automatically on the anniversary of purchase. We email a reminder 7 days before renewal. Monthly plans renew on the same day each month.

Downgrades
Switching from annual to monthly takes effect at the next renewal date.

Refund method
Refunds are returned to the original payment method within 10 business days. Purchases made through a mobile app store are subject to that store's refund rules and must be requested from the store directly.

Data after cancellation
Your notes remain available in read-only mode on the Free plan. Free accounts are limited to 3 notebooks; additional notebooks remain viewable but cannot be edited.
response: You're outside the 14-day full-refund window, so the prorated rule applies. The unused full calendar months after 20 April are May through December, which is 8 months at $12, or $96. After the $15 early-termination fee, you'd get $79 back.

question: We're on the Orbitline Business tier at $8,000 a month, and our measured uptime last month was 98.7%. What credit can we claim, and how long do we have to claim it?
documents:
Orbitline Data Platform - Service Level Agreement (Schedule B to the Master Subscription Agreement)

1. Uptime commitment
Orbitline will make the Platform available with the following Monthly Uptime Percentage, by subscription tier:
Standard: 99.5%
Business: 99.9%
Enterprise: 99.95%

2. Service credits
If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below the commitment for the Customer's tier, the Customer is eligible for a service credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly subscription fee for the affected month:

Monthly Uptime Percentage                       Credit (Business and Enterprise)   Credit (Standard)
Below commitment but at or above 99.0%          10%                                5%
Below 99.0% but at or above 95.0%               25%                                10%
Below 95.0%                                     50%                                25%

3. Claiming credits
The Customer must submit a credit request to support@orbitline.example within 30 calendar days after the end of the month in which the shortfall occurred, including the dates and times of the unavailability. Credits are applied to the next invoice and have no cash value. Total credits in any month may not exceed 50% of that month's subscription fee.

4. Exclusions
Unavailability does not count toward the Monthly Uptime Percentage if it results from (a) scheduled maintenance announced at least 72 hours in advance, limited to 8 hours per month; (b) the Customer's equipment, software or network; (c) suspension under Section 9 of the Master Subscription Agreement; or (d) force majeure events.

5. Sole remedy
Service credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the uptime commitment, except that the Customer may terminate for convenience if uptime falls below 95.0% in any two consecutive months.
response: At 98.7% uptime you fall in the 'below 99.0% but at or above 95.0%' band, which gives Business customers a 25% credit, or $2,000. Submit your claim within 30 business days after the end of the month, including the dates and times of the outage. Credits are applied to the next invoice.
explanation: The deadline is 30 calendar days after month end, not 30 business days.

question: Our Virelle Order Form has an Effective Date of 1 July 2024 and a 36-month initial term. What's the last date we can send a non-renewal notice, and how much could fees go up if we let it renew?
documents:
Virelle Payroll Cloud - Master Subscription Agreement (excerpt: Sections 4 and 11)

4. Term, Renewal and Fees
4.1 Initial Term. The Initial Term of each Order Form begins on the Effective Date stated in that Order Form and continues for the number of months stated in it (if none is stated, 12 months).
4.2 Renewal. Unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term, each Order Form renews automatically for successive renewal terms of 12 months.
4.3 Renewal pricing. Fees for a renewal term may increase by no more than the lesser of (a) 5% or (b) the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding 12 months, applied to the fees for the immediately preceding term. Virelle will notify Customer of any increase at least 120 days before the end of the current term.
4.4 Payment. Fees are invoiced annually in advance and are due within 30 days of the invoice date. Late amounts accrue interest at 1% per month.

11. Termination and Data
11.1 Termination for cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 30 days after receiving written notice describing the breach.
11.2 Effect of termination. On termination for Virelle's uncured breach, Virelle will refund any prepaid fees covering the remainder of the term after the effective date of termination.
11.3 Data export. For 60 days after termination or expiry, Customer may export its data using the standard export tools at no additional charge. After this 60-day period, Virelle will delete Customer data from production systems within 30 days and from backups within a further 90 days.
11.4 Notices. Notices of non-renewal or breach must be sent to legal@virelle.example and to the Customer's account executive.
response: The initial term ends on 30 June 2027, and non-renewal notice must be given at least 90 days before then, so by 1 April 2027. On renewal, fees can rise by no more than the lesser of 5% or the 12-month CPI change, and Virelle must tell you about any increase at least 90 days before the term ends.
explanation: Virelle must notify price increases at least 120 days before the term ends; 90 days is the customer's non-renewal notice period.

question: We're on Kestrel's Essential support plan. We logged a Severity 1 case through the portal at 17:00 on a Friday (no public holidays coming up). By when at the latest should we get a first response?
documents:
Kestrel Helpdesk Suite - Support Policy (version 3.2)

Support plans
Kestrel offers two support plans. Essential support is included with every subscription. Premier support is an add-on priced at 20% of annual subscription fees.

Support hours
Essential: business hours, 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday in the customer's primary time zone, excluding public holidays.
Premier: 24x7 for Severity 1; business hours (as above) for Severity 2-4.

Severity definitions
Severity 1 - Production service is down or unusable for all users, with no workaround.
Severity 2 - Major function impaired for many users; a workaround may exist.
Severity 3 - Minor function impaired or a single user affected.
Severity 4 - Questions, documentation and feature requests.

Initial response targets
Severity   Essential               Premier
1          4 business hours        30 minutes (24x7)
2          8 business hours        2 business hours
3          2 business days         1 business day
4          5 business days         3 business days

Response targets are measured from the time a case is logged through the support portal or by phone. Cases sent by email are logged when they are triaged, which may take up to 1 business hour.

Escalation
Premier customers have a named Technical Account Manager (TAM) and may escalate any open case to the TAM. Essential customers may escalate Severity 1 and 2 cases to the duty manager by phone.

Targets are goals, not guarantees; no service credits apply to support response times. Uptime credits are governed by the Kestrel SLA.
response: By 11:00 Monday: the 4-business-hour Severity 1 target for Essential counts one hour on Friday (17:00-18:00) and three on Monday morning. You can also escalate the case to the duty manager by phone.

response: Essential support covers Severity 1 with an initial response target of 4 business hours, counted only between 08:00 and 18:00 on weekdays. Since you logged the case at 17:00 on Friday, one hour counts on Friday and the rest on Monday, so expect a response by 10:00 on Monday.
explanation: 1 hour on Friday leaves 3 business hours from 08:00 Monday, giving 11:00, not 10:00.

question: Under our DPA with Saltmarsh, if they add a new subprocessor, how much notice do we get, how long do we have to object, and can we get out of the contract if we're not happy?
documents:
Data Processing Addendum (DPA) between Customer and Saltmarsh Analytics B.V. - Sections 6 to 9

6. Subprocessors
6.1 Customer grants a general authorisation for Saltmarsh to engage the subprocessors listed at saltmarsh.example/subprocessors.
6.2 Saltmarsh will notify Customer of any new or replacement subprocessor at least 30 days before that subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data, by email to Customer's designated privacy contact.
6.3 Customer may object to a new subprocessor on reasonable data-protection grounds by written notice within 14 days of receiving Saltmarsh's notification. The parties will discuss the objection in good faith.
6.4 If an objection cannot be resolved within 30 days of the objection, Customer may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for those Services.

7. Personal data breaches
7.1 Saltmarsh will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Customer Personal Data.
7.2 The notification will describe the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned, likely consequences, and measures taken.

8. Audits
8.1 Customer may audit Saltmarsh's compliance with this DPA once in any 12-month period, on at least 30 days' written notice, during normal business hours.
8.2 Audits are at Customer's cost, except where the audit reveals a material breach of this DPA, in which case Saltmarsh will reimburse Customer's reasonable audit costs.
8.3 Saltmarsh may satisfy audit requests by providing its current ISO 27001 certificate and most recent SOC 2 Type II report, unless a supervisory authority requires a direct audit.

Within 30 days after the end of the Services, Saltmarsh will, at Customer's choice, return or delete Customer Personal Data, unless retention is required by law.

explanation: Termination is only available if the objection cannot be resolved within 30 days, a condition the answer omits.

question: We're on Lumenrail Growth. We sent 640,000 message segments in March 2026 but only 420,000 in February. How much overage do we owe for March, and on which invoice will it show up?
documents:

Customer: Pellworth Retail Group
Subscription Start Date: 1 January 2026          Term: 12 months
All amounts are in US dollars (USD) and exclude taxes.

Plan            Monthly fee   Included messages per month   Overage rate (per message)
Starter         $300          100,000                       $0.0030
Growth          $1,200        500,000                       $0.0021   <- selected plan

Usage terms
1. Included messages are allocated per calendar month. Unused included messages expire at the end of each calendar month and do not roll over.

3. Overage is calculated per calendar month at the overage rate for the Customer's plan.

Invoicing

Plan changes
Customer may upgrade to a higher plan at any time, effective from the next calendar month. Downgrades take effect at the next renewal.

Rate limits
Growth: 200 messages per second. Higher limits are available on request.

This Order Form is governed by the Lumenrail Terms of Service.

explanation: The Growth overage rate is $0.0021 per message, not per thousand messages.

question: I have Harbourline Plus. My checked bag was delayed 30 hours on my outbound flight and I had to buy clothes and toiletries. What can I claim?
documents:
Harbourline Travel Protect - Summary of Cover (single-trip policies issued from 1 May 2026)

This summary does not contain the full terms of the policy. Please read the policy wording for full details.

Benefit (per insured person)        Basic        Plus         Premier
Trip cancellation / curtailment     $2,500       $5,000       $10,000
Emergency medical expenses          $250,000     $1,000,000   $5,000,000
Emergency evacuation                $100,000     $250,000     $1,000,000
Lost or damaged baggage             $1,000       $2,000       $3,000
  - single item limit               $250         $500         $750
Baggage delay (12 hours or more)    Not covered  $200         $500
Travel delay (6 hours or more)      $100         $300         $600
Excess per claim                    $250         $100         $0

Baggage delay
If your checked baggage is delayed by an airline for 12 hours or more on your outbound journey, we will reimburse the cost of essential replacement items such as toiletries and clothing, up to the limit shown. Original receipts and the airline's delay confirmation (Property Irregularity Report) are required. The excess does not apply to baggage delay claims.

Pre-existing medical conditions
Pre-existing conditions are excluded on Basic and Plus. On Premier, stable pre-existing conditions are covered if the policy is purchased within 14 days of your initial trip deposit.

Main exclusions
- Hazardous activities, including motorcycling over 125cc, skydiving, and skiing off-piste, unless the Winter Sports add-on is purchased.
- Losses arising from alcohol or drug misuse.
- Cash over $300.
- Travel against government advice.

Claims must be submitted within 60 days of your return home.
response: Your 30-hour outbound delay is well over the 12-hour threshold, so baggage delay cover applies. Harbourline will reimburse anything you bought during the delay, up to $200, and the excess isn't deducted. Submit your receipts and the airline's Property Irregularity Report within 60 days of getting home.
explanation: Only essential replacement items (such as toiletries and clothing) are reimbursed, not any purchase.

question: The hose on my washing machine burst suddenly and soaked the kitchen floor. The flooring repairs are quoted at $6,200 and the house is still liveable. How much would Stonecrake pay, and is there anything else I can claim?
documents:
Stonecrake Home Insurance - Buildings and Contents: Key Facts

Deductibles (excess)
Standard deductible: $500 per claim.
Escape of water claims: $1,000 per claim.
Subsidence claims: $2,500 per claim.
Only one deductible applies when a single incident damages both buildings and contents.

What is covered - escape of water
We cover damage to your buildings and contents caused by water suddenly and accidentally escaping from a fixed water or heating installation, washing machine, dishwasher, fridge-freezer or fish tank. This includes the reasonable cost of finding the source of the leak (trace and access), up to $5,000.

What is not covered - escape of water
- Damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of 14 days or more, or by failed grout or sealant.
- The cost of repairing or replacing the appliance or pipe that caused the leak, unless you hold the optional Appliance Cover and the appliance is less than 5 years old.
- Damage while the home is unoccupied for more than 60 consecutive days.

Alternative accommodation
If your home cannot be lived in following an insured event, we will pay for reasonable alternative accommodation for you and your pets up to $150 per night, for a maximum of 30 nights.

Making a claim
Report the claim within 30 days of discovering the damage. Take photographs before starting repairs, and keep damaged items until our loss adjuster has inspected them or told you they can be thrown away. Emergency repairs to prevent further damage may be carried out straight away; keep the invoices.

Policy limits
Buildings: rebuild cost shown on your schedule. Contents: $75,000, single item limit $2,000 unless specified.
response: A sudden burst from a washing machine is covered as escape of water, which carries a $1,000 deductible. On a $6,200 flooring repair, Stonecrake would pay $5,200. Because the house is still liveable, alternative accommodation wouldn't apply, and replacing the washing machine or hose itself is only covered if you have Appliance Cover and the machine is under 5 years old.

question: The hose on my washing machine burst suddenly and soaked the kitchen floor. The flooring repairs are quoted at $6,200 and the house is still liveable. How much would Stonecrake pay, and is there anything else I can claim?
documents:
Stonecrake Home Insurance - Buildings and Contents: Key Facts

Deductibles (excess)
Standard deductible: $500 per claim.
Escape of water claims: $1,000 per claim.
Subsidence claims: $2,500 per claim.
Only one deductible applies when a single incident damages both buildings and contents.

What is covered - escape of water
We cover damage to your buildings and contents caused by water suddenly and accidentally escaping from a fixed water or heating installation, washing machine, dishwasher, fridge-freezer or fish tank. What is not covered - escape of water
- Damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of 14 days or more, or by failed grout or sealant.
- The cost of repairing or replacing the appliance or pipe that caused the leak, unless you hold the optional Appliance Cover and the appliance is less than 5 years old.
- Damage while the home is unoccupied for more than 60 consecutive days.

Alternative accommodation
If your home cannot be lived in following an insured event, we will pay for reasonable alternative accommodation for you and your pets up to $150 per night, for a maximum of 30 nights.

Making a claim
Report the claim within 30 days of discovering the damage. Take photographs before starting repairs, and keep damaged items until our loss adjuster has inspected them or told you they can be thrown away. Emergency repairs to prevent further damage may be carried out straight away; keep the invoices.

Policy limits
Buildings: rebuild cost shown on your schedule. Contents: $75,000, single item limit $2,000 unless specified.
response: A sudden escape of water from a washing machine is covered. The standard $500 deductible applies, so on a $6,200 flooring repair Stonecrake would pay $5,700. Repairing the machine or hose itself isn't covered unless you hold Appliance Cover and the machine is under 5 years old.
explanation: Escape of water claims carry a $1,000 deductible, so the payout would be $5,200, not $5,700 after a $500 deductible.

question: I have Everyday Checking. This month my balance dropped to $1,200 one day, but I received $800 in direct deposits. Will I be charged the monthly fee? Also, if I end a day overdrawn by $8, is there a fee?
documents:
Harrowgate Community Bank - Personal Checking Fee Schedule (effective 1 October 2026)

Monthly maintenance fees
Account              Monthly fee   How to avoid the fee (any one per statement cycle)
Everyday Checking    $12           Minimum daily balance of $1,500; OR direct deposits totalling $500 or more; OR account holder aged 24 or under
Premier Checking     $25           Combined average daily balance of $15,000 across Harrowgate deposit and investment accounts
Student Checking     $0            Available to students aged 17-24

Overdraft and returned items
Overdraft fee (item paid): $32 per item, maximum 3 fees per business day.
Returned item fee (item not paid): $32 per item.
No overdraft fee is charged if your account is overdrawn by $10 or less at the end of the business day.
Overdraft protection transfer from linked savings: $10 per transfer.

ATMs
Harrowgate and Larchnet network ATMs: free.
Other ATMs: $3 per withdrawal, plus any fee charged by the ATM owner. Premier Checking customers receive refunds of other banks' ATM fees up to $15 per statement cycle.

Wire transfers
Domestic incoming: $15. Domestic outgoing: $25. International outgoing: $45. International incoming: $15.

Other services
Stop payment: $30. Cashier's check: $8 (free for Premier). Paper statements: $2 per month (free for customers aged 65 or over). Replacement debit card: free for the first card each year, then $5.

Fees are subject to change with 30 days' notice.
response: The $12 Everyday Checking fee is waived if you meet any one condition, and direct deposits of $250 or more qualify, so your $800 covers it even though your balance fell below $1,500. And if you're overdrawn by $10 or less at the end of the business day, no overdraft fee is charged.
explanation: The direct-deposit threshold to waive the fee is $500, not $250.

question: I'm going to a conference in a high-cost city from Monday to Wednesday (two nights). The conference provides lunch on Tuesday. What's my total meal per diem?
documents:
Ostrell Medical Devices - Domestic Travel Policy: Meals and Incidentals (TRV-03)

Per diem rates
Employees on overnight business travel receive a daily meals and incidentals per diem instead of submitting meal receipts.
Standard locations: $65 per day.
High-cost cities (listed in Appendix A): $85 per day.

First and last days of travel
On the day of departure and the day of return, the per diem is 75% of the daily rate.

Meals provided
When a meal is provided at no cost to the employee (for example, by a conference, client or hotel package), deduct the following amount from that day's per diem: breakfast $15, lunch $20, dinner $30. Deductions apply to full days of travel only; no deduction is made from the 75% first-day and last-day amounts. Continental breakfasts included in a standard hotel rate are not deducted.

Receipts
Receipts are not required for per diem. Hotel, airfare and ground transportation require itemised receipts.

Lodging
Hotels must be booked through the corporate travel portal. The nightly cap is $210 in standard locations and $320 in high-cost cities, excluding taxes. Exceptions require VP approval before booking.

Alcohol
Alcohol is not reimbursable and is not covered by per diem.

Submitting expenses
Submit expense reports within 30 days of returning. Reports submitted more than 90 days after travel will not be reimbursed.

Day trips
No per diem is paid for travel that does not include an overnight stay. Meals on day trips are reimbursed only when a client is present, with receipts.
response: The high-cost city rate is $85 per day. Monday and Wednesday are your departure and return days, so each gets 75%, which is $63.75. Tuesday is a full day with lunch provided, so $20 is deducted, leaving $65. Your total per diem is $192.50, and you don't need meal receipts.

question: On a regular Tuesday I drove my own car from home to a client site and back, 180 km in total. My normal round-trip commute to the office is 40 km, and I've logged about 1,200 business km so far this year. How much can I claim?
documents:
Maplerigg Consulting Inc. (Canada) - Vehicle and Ground Transportation Guidelines

1. Personal vehicle use
Employees who use a personal vehicle for business travel are reimbursed per kilometre:
- C$0.70 per km for the first 5,000 business kilometres in a calendar year
- C$0.64 per km for business kilometres beyond 5,000 in the same year
The per-kilometre rate covers fuel, insurance, maintenance and depreciation. No additional fuel claims are permitted for personal vehicles.

2. Commuting deduction
Travel between home and your regular office is personal commuting and is not reimbursable. When a business trip starts or ends at home on a day you would normally work at the office, deduct your normal round-trip commuting distance from the business kilometres claimed. On weekends and statutory holidays, no deduction is required.

3. Parking and tolls
Business parking and highway tolls are reimbursed with receipts. Parking at your regular office is not reimbursed.

4. Rental vehicles
Rentals must be booked through the travel portal in the compact class or smaller, unless three or more employees are travelling together, in which case a mid-size vehicle is permitted. Refuel the vehicle before returning it; fuel purchased for rental vehicles is reimbursed with receipts. Prepaid fuel options are not reimbursed.

5. Taxis and ride-hailing
Permitted when public transit is impractical. Receipts are required for any fare over C$20.

6. Claims
Mileage claims must include the date, start and end points, purpose, and kilometres driven. Submit claims within 30 days of the trip.
response: You're under the 5,000 km annual threshold, so the C$0.70 per km rate applies. Because the trip started from home rather than the office, you don't need to deduct your normal commute, so you can claim the full 180 km, or C$126.00. Remember that fuel isn't claimable separately for your own car.
explanation: On a normal workday a trip starting and ending at home requires deducting the 40 km commute, so the claim is 140 km x C$0.70 = C$98.00.

question: Do I have to change my Grenmoor password every 90 days? And if I mistype it a few times, when do I get locked out and for how long?
documents:
Grenmoor Biotech - Information Security Standard IT-SEC-02: Authentication

Scope
Applies to all employees, contractors and service accounts accessing Grenmoor systems.

1. Passwords for user accounts
1.1 Minimum length is 14 characters. Passphrases of four or more unrelated words are encouraged.
1.2 Passwords must not contain your username, the company name, or any password used in the last 10 changes.
1.3 Grenmoor does not require periodic password changes for user accounts. Passwords must be changed immediately if compromise is suspected or if the IT Service Desk instructs you to do so.
1.4 Passwords must be stored only in the approved password manager (Grenmoor Vault). Writing passwords down or storing them in browsers is prohibited.

2. Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
2.1 MFA is required for all remote access, email, and cloud applications.
2.2 Privileged accounts (domain administrators, production database administrators) must use a FIDO2 hardware security key. Push notifications and SMS codes are not permitted for privileged accounts.
2.3 SMS codes are permitted for standard user accounts only as a backup method.

3. Account lockout
After 10 consecutive failed sign-in attempts, the account is locked for 15 minutes. Repeated lockouts within 24 hours are reported to the Security Operations Centre.

4. Service accounts
Service account passwords must be at least 32 characters, generated randomly, and rotated every 180 days or when a person with knowledge of the password leaves the team.

5. Sharing
Credentials must never be shared, including with managers or IT staff. The IT Service Desk will never ask for your password.

Exceptions to this standard require written approval from the CISO.
response: No, Grenmoor doesn't require periodic password changes for user accounts. You only need to change it immediately if you suspect it's been compromised or if the IT Service Desk tells you to. Your account locks after 10 consecutive failed sign-in attempts, and the lockout lasts 15 minutes.

question: I need to send our Confidential pricing sheet to a partner who has signed an NDA. Can I email it to them, and can I put a copy on a USB stick to take to their office?

Ashcombe Engineering Ltd - Data Classification and Handling Standard (ISP-07)

Public: approved for public release (marketing materials, published reports).
Internal: general business information not intended for the public (org charts, internal announcements).

Restricted: highly sensitive information subject to legal or regulatory protection (employee health and payroll data, export-controlled technical data, M&A plans).

Sharing outside Ashcombe
Public: no restrictions.
Internal: may be shared with contractors and partners who have a business need.
Confidential: may be shared externally only with a party under a signed NDA, and only through Vaultline Share (the approved encrypted file-sharing service). Email attachments to external recipients are not permitted for Confidential data.
Restricted: must not be shared externally without prior written approval from the CISO and the data owner. Approved transfers use Vaultline Share with recipient identity verification.

Removable media
USB storage devices are blocked by default. Internal and Confidential data may be copied only to company-issued encrypted USB drives requested through the IT Service Desk. Restricted data must never be copied to removable media.

Personal accounts and devices
Forwarding any Internal, Confidential or Restricted data to personal email or personal cloud storage is prohibited.

Labelling
Documents classified Confidential or Restricted must carry the classification label in the header or footer.

Breaches
Suspected mishandling must be reported to security@ashcombe.example within 24 hours.
response: Not by email. Use Vaultline Share, which is allowed for Confidential data with an NDA in place. A USB copy is only allowed on a company-issued encrypted drive from the IT Service Desk.

question: I clicked a link in what looks like a phishing email and typed my password into the page. What should I do and how quickly?
documents:
Brightwick Credit Union - Security Incident Reporting Procedure (SEC-PROC-11)

What to report
Report any actual or suspected security incident, including: phishing emails; clicking a suspicious link or opening a suspicious attachment; entering credentials on an unexpected login page; lost or stolen devices; malware warnings; and unauthorised access to member data.

How to report
- Phishing emails you have NOT interacted with: use the 'Report Phish' button in your mail client. This removes the email from your inbox and sends it to the Security Operations Centre (SOC). No further action is needed.
- If you clicked a link, opened an attachment, or entered credentials: call the SOC hotline on extension 7777 within 1 hour of realising, then use the 'Report Phish' button.
- Lost or stolen laptops, phones or access badges: report to the SOC hotline within 4 hours of discovering the loss.

If you entered your password on a suspicious page
1. Change your network password immediately from a different, trusted device.
2. Do not sign in to any other systems from the affected device until the SOC clears it.
3. Leave the affected device powered on but disconnect it from Wi-Fi and unplug any network cable, so the SOC can investigate.

What not to do
- Do not forward suspicious emails to colleagues, including to warn them; the SOC will issue alerts if needed.
- Do not try to investigate the link or attachment yourself.
- Do not delete the email manually; the Report Phish button handles removal.

No blame
Brightwick operates a no-blame reporting culture. Prompt reporting of mistakes is expected and valued.
response: Ring the SOC hotline on extension 7777 within 1 hour of realising what happened, and then use the 'Report Phish' button. Change your network password immediately from a different, trusted device. Keep the affected device powered on but disconnected from the network, and run a full antivirus scan on it while you wait for the SOC.
explanation: The procedure says nothing about running an antivirus scan; it tells staff not to investigate themselves.

question: My Bellwyn dental coverage started on 1 February 2026 and I had no dental insurance before. My dentist says I need a crown in December 2026, costing about $1,200. Will the plan cover it?
documents:
Bellwyn Dental Plan - Benefit Summary (Individual and Family Plans, plan year 2026)

Coverage by service category
Category                      Examples                                          Plan pays    Deductible applies?   Waiting period
Preventive                    Exams, cleanings (2 per year), bitewing X-rays    100%         No                    None
Basic                         Fillings, simple extractions, root canals         80%          Yes                   6 months
Major                         Crowns, bridges, dentures, implants               50%          Yes                   12 months
Orthodontics (under age 19)   Braces, aligners                                  50%          No                    12 months

Deductible
$50 per person per plan year, maximum $150 per family. The deductible does not apply to Preventive services or Orthodontics.

Annual maximum
The plan pays up to $1,500 per person per plan year for Preventive, Basic and Major services combined. Orthodontics has a separate lifetime maximum of $1,000 per eligible child.

Waiting periods
Waiting periods are counted from the member's coverage effective date. Services received before the end of the waiting period are not covered, even if treatment was recommended after enrollment. Waiting periods are waived for members who had continuous dental coverage for at least 12 months immediately before enrolling, with no gap of more than 63 days; proof of prior coverage must be submitted within 30 days of enrollment.

Missing tooth clause
Replacement of a tooth that was missing before the coverage effective date is not covered for the first 24 months of coverage.

Network
Members may see any dentist. In-network dentists accept Bellwyn's negotiated fees; out-of-network dentists may bill the difference between their fee and Bellwyn's allowed amount.

Pre-treatment estimates
For any treatment expected to cost more than $500, we recommend asking your dentist to submit a pre-treatment estimate.
response: Crowns are classed as Major services, which have a 12-month waiting period counted from your coverage effective date. For you that waiting period ends on 1 January 2027, so a crown in December 2026 wouldn't be covered. Because you had no prior dental coverage, the waiting-period waiver doesn't apply.
explanation: 12 months from 1 February 2026 ends on 1 February 2027, not 1 January 2027.

question: I'm a Standard customer at Corbridge and want to send the equivalent of $12,000 to a euro account in Europe using online banking. What will it cost me?
documents:
Corbridge Savings Bank - International Payments: Fees and Exchange Rates (personal customers)

Exchange rate margin
When you send money in a foreign currency, we convert it at the Corbridge exchange rate, which includes a margin over the mid-market rate. The margin depends on the amount converted (in US dollars):
Amount converted         Margin
Under $10,000            2.50%
$10,000 to $49,999       1.75%
$50,000 or more          1.00%

Transfer fees (per payment)
Channel                  Standard customers   Gold customers
Online or mobile app     $25                  Free
Branch or phone          $40                  $20

Gold status applies to customers with combined balances of $100,000 or more across Corbridge accounts.

Charges from other banks
Intermediary and recipient banks may deduct their own charges. Choose the 'OUR' option to pay these charges for the recipient for an additional $20 flat fee; otherwise charges are shared ('SHA').

Cut-off times
Payments submitted by 15:00 Eastern Time on a business day are sent the same day. Payments in euro and pounds sterling usually arrive within 1 business day; other currencies within 2-4 business days.

Limits
Online and mobile app: up to $50,000 per day. Larger amounts must be arranged by phone or in branch.

Incoming international payments
$15 per payment, deducted from the amount received. Free for Gold customers.

Cancellations and returns
A payment can be cancelled free of charge before it is sent. Recalls after sending cost $30 and are not guaranteed.
response: Expect about $235: a 1.75% margin on $12,000 ($210) plus the $25 online transfer fee for Standard customers. Submit it before 15:00 Eastern on a business day and a euro payment usually arrives within 1 business day.

question: I'm a director at Harrowfield. My trip to Singapore has two daytime legs of 5 hours 40 minutes and 4 hours 10 minutes, with a 3-hour layover. Can I fly business class?
documents:
Harrowfield Pharmaceuticals - Global Travel Policy, Section 4: Air Travel

4.1 Booking
All flights must be booked through Harrowfield's travel management company, Compass Route Travel, at least 14 days before departure where possible. Bookings made less than 7 days before departure require a short justification in the booking tool.

4.2 Class of travel
The permitted class of travel is based on the total scheduled flight time of the journey in each direction, excluding time spent on layovers:
Total scheduled flight time   Permitted class
Under 6 hours                 Economy
6 to 10 hours                 Premium economy
Over 10 hours                 Business
Employees at Vice President level and above may book business class on any flight of 4 hours or more.
Overnight 'red-eye' flights of 5 hours or more may be booked in premium economy regardless of duration band.

4.3 Lowest logical fare
Travellers must choose the lowest logical fare within the permitted class, defined as the cheapest fare with no more than one additional connection and a total journey time no more than 2 hours longer than the fastest option.

4.4 Upgrades
Personal loyalty points may be used to upgrade at the traveller's own expense. Paid upgrades are not reimbursable.

4.5 Baggage
One checked bag is reimbursable on any flight. Additional bags require a business reason (e.g., carrying product samples or equipment).

4.6 Loyalty programmes
Employees may keep airline miles earned on business travel, but the choice of airline must not be influenced by loyalty programme membership.

4.7 Approval
Business class bookings by employees below Vice President level require approval from their department head before ticketing.
response: Class of travel is based on scheduled flight time excluding layovers, and your two legs add up to 9 hours 30 minutes. That falls in the 6-10 hour band, so you're entitled to premium economy, not business. Business class on shorter flights is reserved for Vice Presidents and above.

question: On 3 March I accidentally paid a $40 personal purchase with my Sablewood card. I've also lost the receipt for a $60 taxi ride, and it's my first missing receipt this quarter. What do I need to do?
documents:
Sablewood Media Group - Corporate Card and Receipts Policy (FIN-09)

1. Use of the corporate card
The Sablewood corporate card may be used only for business expenses. Personal purchases are not permitted. If a personal charge is made by mistake, the cardholder must report it in the expense system and repay Sablewood within 15 calendar days of the transaction date, by bank transfer to the account shown in the expense system.

2. Receipts
An itemised receipt is required for every expense of $25 or more. For hotel stays, the itemised folio is required regardless of amount. Credit card slips without item detail are not accepted as receipts for meals.

3. Missing receipts
If a receipt is lost, the cardholder may submit a Missing Receipt Declaration in place of the receipt. Missing Receipt Declarations are limited to:
- expenses of $75 or less each, and
- no more than 2 declarations per calendar quarter.
Expenses above $75 without a receipt require approval from the cardholder's Finance Business Partner.

4. Monthly reconciliation
Cardholders must reconcile all transactions for a statement period in the expense system by the 10th of the following month. Managers must approve reconciled reports within 5 business days.

5. Non-compliance
If reconciliation is late for two consecutive months, the card is suspended until all outstanding items are cleared. Repeated personal use may lead to card withdrawal and disciplinary action.

6. Card limits
Standard card limit: $5,000 per month. Temporary increases for events or extended travel can be requested through Finance at least 5 business days in advance.
response: Repay the $40 by 18 March after flagging it in the expense system. The $60 taxi can be covered by a Missing Receipt Declaration, which is allowed for expenses up to $75, up to twice per calendar quarter.

question: I'd like to work from Portugal for three weeks (Monday to Friday each week) in May, and I haven't worked abroad yet this year. Is that allowed, and can I use the hotel Wi-Fi?
documents:
Corran & Vale LLP - Remote and International Working: IT Security Requirements (IT-POL-12)

1. Devices
Firm work must be done on firm-issued laptops, which have full-disk encryption, endpoint protection and automatic updates enforced. Personal computers may not be used to access client files. Personal phones may be used for email and calendar only through the managed Corran Mail app, which can be remotely wiped by IT.

2. Networks
Home broadband is acceptable. On any network the firm does not control, including hotel, airport, cafe and client guest Wi-Fi, you must connect to the firm VPN (Corran SecureLink) before accessing any firm system. Personal mobile hotspots are permitted with the VPN.

3. Working from abroad
Employees may work remotely from outside their home country for up to 20 working days per calendar year. Each trip requires approval from your line manager and the IT Security team, requested through the service portal at least 10 working days before departure. Working from the countries on the Restricted Destinations List (available on the intranet) is not permitted under any circumstances.

4. Physical security
Do not leave devices unattended in public places or in vehicles. Use a privacy screen when working in public spaces. Lock your screen whenever you step away.

5. Printing
Printing client documents outside firm offices is not permitted.

6. Lost devices
Report lost or stolen devices to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 2 hours.

Breaches of this policy may result in disciplinary action.
response: Three weeks of Monday-to-Friday work is 15 working days, so you're within the 20-working-day annual allowance and would have 6 days left for the rest of the year. You'll need line manager and IT Security approval through the service portal at least 10 working days before departure. Hotel Wi-Fi is allowed if you connect to the Corran SecureLink VPN first.
explanation: 20 - 15 leaves 5 working days, not 6.

question: We're on Tessellate Live - Standard. What's our rate limit, what happens if we go over it, and what's the most records we can get per page from GET /v2/payments?
documents:
Tessellate Payments API v2 - Rate Limits and Pagination

Rate limits
Requests are rate-limited per API key using a token bucket. Limits depend on the environment and your plan:

Environment / plan   Sustained limit        Burst capacity
Sandbox              25 requests/second     50 requests
Live - Standard      100 requests/second    200 requests
Live - Plus          400 requests/second    800 requests

Burst capacity lets you briefly exceed the sustained limit; the bucket refills at the sustained rate.

When you exceed the limit, the API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Requests rejected with 429 still count toward your rate limit, so retrying immediately in a loop will extend the throttling. We recommend exponential backoff with jitter, starting at the Retry-After value.

Every response includes these headers:
X-RateLimit-Limit       your sustained limit per second
X-RateLimit-Remaining   tokens left in the bucket
X-RateLimit-Reset       Unix timestamp when the bucket will be full

The /v2/reports endpoints have a separate limit of 5 requests per minute on all plans.

Pagination
List endpoints (for example GET /v2/payments, GET /v2/refunds, GET /v2/customers) use cursor-based pagination.
Parameters:
limit            number of objects to return; default 20, minimum 1, maximum 100
starting_after   cursor: the ID of the last object from the previous page
ending_before    cursor: the ID of the first object from the previous page (for paging backwards)

The response includes has_more (boolean) and data (array). To fetch the next page, pass the ID of the last object in data as starting_after. Do not combine starting_after and ending_before in one request; the API will return HTTP 400.

Objects are returned in reverse chronological order (newest first) by created timestamp. Cursors do not expire, but objects deleted after you fetched a page will not appear in later pages.

Example
GET /v2/payments?limit=50&starting_after=pay_8Hq2LmX

Support
Plus customers can request a temporary limit increase for planned events (for example, a product launch) by contacting support at least 5 business days in advance.
response: Your sustained limit on Live - Standard is 400 requests per second, with a burst capacity of 800. If you exceed it you'll receive HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and a Retry-After header giving the seconds to wait. You can request up to 100 objects per page from GET /v2/payments using the limit parameter.
explanation: 400/s with 800 burst is the Live - Plus limit; Live - Standard is 100/s with 200 burst.

question: If our webhook endpoint is down and Tessellate's first delivery attempt for an event fails at 09:00, when will the final automatic retry happen? Also, how quickly do we need to respond once we're back up?
documents:
Tessellate Payments API v2 - Webhooks Guide

Overview
Webhooks notify your server when events happen in your account, such as payment.succeeded, payment.failed, refund.created and dispute.opened. Configure endpoints in Dashboard > Developers > Webhooks. Each endpoint can subscribe to specific event types.

Responding to webhooks
Your endpoint must return a 2xx HTTP status code within 10 seconds of receiving the request. Any other status code, a redirect, or a timeout is treated as a failed delivery. Do the minimum work needed to acknowledge the event (for example, store it in a queue) and process it asynchronously.

Retries
If a delivery fails, Tessellate retries it up to 5 times. Each retry is scheduled after a fixed interval measured from the previous attempt:

Retry   Interval after previous attempt
1       5 minutes
2       30 minutes
3       2 hours
4       6 hours
5       12 hours

If all retries fail, the event is marked as failed and no further automatic attempts are made. If deliveries to an endpoint fail continuously for 3 days, the endpoint is automatically disabled and the account owner is emailed.

Verifying signatures
Each request includes a Tessellate-Signature header containing a timestamp (t) and an HMAC-SHA256 signature (v1) computed over the timestamp and the raw request body using your endpoint's signing secret. Reject requests whose signature does not match, and reject requests whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes older than your server's current time to prevent replay attacks.

Ordering and duplicates
Tessellate does not guarantee that events are delivered in the order they were created. The same event may occasionally be delivered more than once; use the event id to make your processing idempotent.

Testing
Use the Tessellate CLI command 'tessellate listen' to forward sandbox events to a local server. Sandbox and live endpoints use different signing secrets.

Webhooks notify your server when events happen in your account, such as payment.succeeded, payment.failed, refund.created and dispute.opened. Configure endpoints in Dashboard > Developers > Webhooks. Each endpoint can subscribe to specific event types.

Responding to webhooks
Your endpoint must return a 2xx HTTP status code within 10 seconds of receiving the request. Any other status code, a redirect, or a timeout is treated as a failed delivery. Do the minimum work needed to acknowledge the event (for example, store it in a queue) and process it asynchronously.

Retries
If a delivery fails, Tessellate retries it up to 5 times. Each retry is scheduled after a fixed interval measured from the previous attempt:

Retry   Interval after previous attempt
1       5 minutes
2       30 minutes
3       2 hours
4       6 hours
5       12 hours

Each request includes a Tessellate-Signature header containing a timestamp (t) and an HMAC-SHA256 signature (v1) computed over the timestamp and the raw request body using your endpoint's signing secret. Reject requests whose signature does not match, and reject requests whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes older than your server's current time to prevent replay attacks.

Ordering and duplicates
Tessellate does not guarantee that events are delivered in the order they were created. The same event may occasionally be delivered more than once; use the event id to make your processing idempotent.

Use the Tessellate CLI command 'tessellate listen' to forward sandbox events to a local server. Sandbox and live endpoints use different signing secrets.

question: For the Brindle API using the authorization code flow, how long does an access token last, and can I reuse the same refresh token more than once?
documents:
Brindle HR Platform API - Authentication (OAuth 2.0)

Brindle uses OAuth 2.0 for all API access. Two grant types are supported:
- Client credentials, for server-to-server integrations that act on behalf of your organisation.
- Authorization code with PKCE, for applications that act on behalf of an individual Brindle user.

Token endpoint
POST https://auth.brindle.example/oauth/token

Access tokens
Access tokens are JWTs valid for 60 minutes from issue. The token response includes expires_in, given in seconds (3600). Send the token in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>'. Requests with an expired token return HTTP 401 with error code token_expired.

Refresh tokens (authorization code flow only)
Refresh tokens are valid for 30 days from issue. Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate: each time you exchange a refresh token, you receive a new access token and a new refresh token, and the old refresh token is invalidated. If a refresh token that has already been used is presented again, Brindle treats this as possible token theft and revokes every token in that token family; the user must sign in again.
The client credentials grant does not issue refresh tokens; request a new access token when the current one expires.

Scopes
Request only the scopes you need. Common scopes:
employees.read     read employee profiles
employees.write    create and update employee profiles
payroll.read       read payslips and pay runs (requires admin consent)
timeoff.write      create and approve leave requests

Environments
Sandbox tokens are issued by https://auth.sandbox.brindle.example and are not valid against production APIs, and vice versa.

Limits
Each user may have at most 10 active refresh tokens per client application. Issuing an eleventh revokes the oldest.

Clock skew
Brindle allows up to 60 seconds of clock skew when validating token timestamps.
response: Access tokens last 60 minutes, which the token response expresses as expires_in: 3600 seconds. Refresh tokens are single-use: each exchange returns a new access token and a new refresh token, and the old one is invalidated. Each refresh token is valid for up to 30 hours from issue if it isn't used.
explanation: Refresh tokens are valid for 30 days, not 30 hours.

question: We still call Corvid Maps v2 Routes and read the 'distance' field. When will v2 stop working, and what do we need to change about distance?
documents:
Corvid Maps Platform - API v2 Deprecation and Migration to v3

Timeline
- 1 October 2026: API v3 generally available.
- 1 January 2027: v2 responses begin including 'Deprecation' and 'Sunset' HTTP headers.
- 3 February 2027 and 3 March 2027: scheduled 2-hour brownouts of v2, from 14:00 to 16:00 UTC, during which v2 requests return HTTP 410 Gone.
- 31 March 2027: v2 is permanently shut down. After this date all v2 requests return HTTP 410 Gone.

Breaking changes in v3
1. Base URL: https://api.corvidmaps.example/v3/ (was /v2/).
2. Authentication: API keys move from the 'key' query parameter to the 'X-Corvid-Key' header. Query-parameter keys are rejected.
3. Coordinates: the top-level 'lat' and 'lng' fields are replaced by a nested object 'location': {'latitude': ..., 'longitude': ...}.
4. Distances: the Routes endpoint returns 'distance' in metres as an integer. In v2, 'distance' was returned in kilometres as a decimal.
5. Durations: 'duration' is now returned in seconds (unchanged from v2), but 'duration_in_traffic' is only included when the request sets departure_time.
6. Geocoding: the /geocode/reverse endpoint is renamed /reverse-geocode.

Unchanged in v3
Rate limits, billing SKUs and prices, and the Places endpoint request format are unchanged.

Migration help
Our migration guide includes a field-mapping table and code samples for the JavaScript, Python and Java SDKs. SDK versions 5.0 and above call v3 by default; versions 4.x call v2 and must be upgraded.

Questions: developer-support@corvidmaps.example.
response: Corvid Maps v2 will be shut down permanently on 3 March 2027, after which v2 requests return HTTP 410 Gone. In v3 the Routes endpoint returns 'distance' in metres as an integer, whereas v2 returned kilometres as a decimal, so you'll need to update how you read that field.
explanation: 3 March 2027 is the second brownout date; the permanent shutdown is 31 March 2027.

question: I'm an adult and took my first Veltoprofen tablet at 7 am with breakfast. When is the earliest I can take the next one, and how many can I take in total within 24 hours?
documents:
PACKAGE LEAFLET: INFORMATION FOR THE PATIENT
Veltoprofen 200 mg film-coated tablets (fictional product, for illustration only)

Read all of this leaflet carefully before you start taking this medicine. Keep this leaflet; you may need to read it again.

1. What Veltoprofen is and what it is used for
Veltoprofen belongs to a group of medicines called non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). It is used for the short-term relief of mild to moderate pain, such as headache, dental pain, period pain and muscular pain, and to reduce fever.

2. Do not take Veltoprofen
- if you are allergic to veltoprofen or other NSAIDs;
- if you have, or have had, a stomach ulcer or bleeding;
- if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy;
- if you have severe heart, liver or kidney failure.
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking Veltoprofen if you have asthma, high blood pressure, or take blood-thinning medicines (anticoagulants) or other NSAIDs.

3. How to take Veltoprofen
Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet with water, with or after food. If needed, take another tablet after at least 6 hours. Leave at least 6 hours between doses. Do not take more than 3 tablets in any 24-hour period.
Not for children under 12 years.
Do not take for more than 10 days for pain or 3 days for fever without speaking to your doctor.

If you take more than you should: contact a doctor or the nearest hospital emergency department immediately, even if you feel well.

4. Possible side effects
Common (may affect up to 1 in 10 people): indigestion, nausea, heartburn.
Uncommon (up to 1 in 100): headache, dizziness, skin rash.
Stop taking Veltoprofen and seek medical help immediately if you notice black tarry stools, vomit blood, or develop swelling of the face or difficulty breathing.

5. How to store Veltoprofen
Store below 25 degrees C. Keep out of the sight and reach of children.
response: You need to leave at least 6 hours between doses, so the earliest you can take the next tablet is 1 pm. You shouldn't take more than 3 tablets in any 24-hour period, and each one should be taken with water, with or after food.

question: I started using a new Glyvaro pen on 10 May and I'm keeping it at room temperature. By when do I have to throw it away, and how should I store it in the meantime?
documents:
INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE AND STORAGE
Glyvaro 100 units/mL solution for injection in a pre-filled pen (fictional medicine, for illustration only)

Before first use (unopened pens)
Store unopened pens in a refrigerator at 2 to 8 degrees C. Do not freeze. Do not store next to the freezer compartment or a cooling element. Unopened pens can be used until the expiry date printed on the label and carton (after 'EXP') when stored this way.

After first use (pen in use)
Once you start using a pen, keep it at room temperature, below 30 degrees C, and away from direct heat and light. Do not put an in-use pen back in the refrigerator. An in-use pen must be discarded 28 days after first use, even if it still contains medicine. Write the date of first use on the pen label to help you remember.

Carrying a spare pen
A spare unopened pen may be kept out of the refrigerator, below 30 degrees C, for up to 28 days; it must then be used within the 28 days or discarded. Record the date it was removed from the refrigerator.

Do not use the pen
- if it has been frozen, even if it has since thawed;
- if the solution is not clear and colourless;
- after the expiry date or after the 28-day in-use period.

Needles
Always attach a new needle for each injection. Remove the needle after each injection and dispose of it in a sharps container. Never share your pen or needles with another person, even if the needle is changed.

Travelling
Keep pens in your hand luggage when flying. Do not place them in checked baggage, where they may freeze.

Ask your pharmacist how to dispose of pens you no longer use.
response: Your pen should be discarded on 7 June, 28 days after you first used it on 10 May, even if it isn't empty. Store it below 30 degrees C away from heat and direct light, and don't put it back in the fridge. If you drop the pen, discard it straight away and start a new one.
explanation: The instructions say nothing about discarding a pen that has been dropped.

question: We're the tenant of Unit 4 at Haldane Business Park. Can we get out of the lease early, and what's the latest date to serve notice?

LEASE OF UNIT 4, HALDANE BUSINESS PARK - PARTICULARS AND BREAK CLAUSE (EXTRACT)

Landlord: Haldane Estates Limited
Tenant: Fenwright Design Studio Limited
Term: 10 years from and including 1 September 2024 (the Term Commencement Date)
Initial rent: $96,000 per year, exclusive of VAT, payable quarterly in advance on the usual quarter days

Clause 7 - Rent review
7.1 The rent will be reviewed on the third and sixth anniversaries of the Term Commencement Date.
7.2 The reviewed rent will be the higher of (a) the rent payable immediately before the review date and (b) the open market rent as agreed or determined under Schedule 3. The rent can never be reduced on review.

9.1 The Tenant may terminate this Lease on 31 August 2029 (the Break Date) by giving the Landlord not less than 9 months' prior written notice.

(a) all rent and service charge due under this Lease up to the Break Date has been paid in full;
(b) the Tenant gives vacant possession of the whole of the Premises; and
(c) the Tenant has paid to the Landlord a sum equal to 3 months' rent at the rate then payable (the Break Premium).
9.3 Time is of the essence for the service of the break notice. Notice served late will be invalid.
9.4 The Landlord has no right to terminate this Lease early except for forfeiture under Clause 12.

response: Yes, there's a tenant break option allowing you to end the lease on 31 August 2029. question: If I pay my rent for 212 Corliss Avenue on the 9th of the month, how much will the late fees be? And could I get a 50-lb Labrador as a pet?

Property: 212 Corliss Avenue, Apt 3C. Landlord: Westbury Lane Properties LLC.

Monthly rent is $1,850, due on the 1st day of each month. Rent may be paid through the resident portal (free), by ACH, or by certified cheque delivered to the leasing office. Personal cheques are not accepted after a returned payment.

Rent received by 11:59 pm on the 5th of the month is considered on time. If rent has not been received by then, an initial late fee of $75 is charged on the 6th. A returned payment fee of $40 applies, in addition to any late fees.

4. Pets
Residents may keep up to 2 pets with the Landlord's prior written approval. Permitted pets are domestic cats and dogs under 40 lb at full adult weight. The following are not permitted: reptiles, rabbits, rodents other than caged hamsters, and any dog breed listed in Schedule 4.
Each approved pet requires:
- a refundable pet deposit of $400, and
- monthly pet rent of $35.
Assistance animals are not pets and are not subject to pet deposits, pet rent or weight limits; requests are handled under the Landlord's reasonable accommodation policy.

5. Pet damage
Damage caused by pets beyond normal wear and tear may be deducted from the pet deposit and, if that is insufficient, from the security deposit.
response: You'd owe $105 in late fees: the $75 initial fee on the 6th and $10 for each of the 7th, 8th and 9th. You can keep up to two pets of any kind with written approval, each requiring a $400 refundable deposit and $35 monthly pet rent, so a Labrador would be fine once approved.
explanation: Only cats and dogs under 40 lb (and caged hamsters) are allowed; a 50-lb Labrador exceeds the weight limit.

question: I have a 36-month Elmstead lease and will return the car with 41,500 miles on it (it was new at delivery). What will the excess mileage charge be, and is there a disposition fee? I'm not planning to get another car from Elmstead.
documents:
Elmstead Motors Finance - Closed-End Vehicle Lease: End-of-Lease Terms (Section 14)

14.1 Mileage allowance
Your lease includes 12,000 miles per year of the lease term (the Mileage Allowance). For a 36-month lease this is 36,000 miles in total. Mileage is measured from the odometer reading recorded on the delivery receipt.

14.2 Excess mileage charge
If the odometer reading at return exceeds the total Mileage Allowance, you will pay $0.20 for each mile over the allowance. Unused miles are not refunded.

14.3 Excess wear and use
At return, the vehicle will be inspected by an independent inspector. You will pay for damage beyond normal wear and use, including: tyres with less than 4/32 inch of tread; dents larger than 2 inches; cracked glass; and missing keys (charged at $250 per key).

14.4 Disposition fee
A disposition fee of $395 is payable when you return the vehicle at lease end. The disposition fee is waived if, within 90 days of returning the vehicle, you lease or finance another new vehicle through Elmstead Motors Finance.

14.5 Purchase option
You may buy the vehicle at lease end for the Purchase Option Price shown in your lease, plus a $300 purchase option fee and applicable taxes. If you purchase the vehicle, the excess mileage charge, excess wear charges and disposition fee do not apply.

14.6 Early termination
You may end the lease early at any time. You will owe the early termination amount described in Section 15, which can be substantial.

14.7 Return
Return the vehicle to any authorised Elmstead dealer with all keys, manuals and accessories. Schedule a pre-return inspection at least 30 days before your lease end date to identify any chargeable damage.
response: You'll be 5,500 miles over your 36,000-mile allowance, which at $0.20 per mile comes to $1,100. The $395 disposition fee applies because you aren't getting another Elmstead vehicle. If you did lease or finance another new vehicle through Elmstead within 90 days, the excess mileage charge would be waived as well.
explanation: Getting another Elmstead vehicle within 90 days only waives the disposition fee; excess mileage is waived only if you purchase the leased vehicle.

question: I placed a $480 Ridgeback order (standard ground) to our warehouse in Ohio at 3:00 pm Central on a Thursday (not a holiday week). What will shipping cost, and what's the earliest it could arrive?
documents:
Ridgeback Industrial Supply - Shipping and Delivery Terms for Business Customers

1. Shipping charges (contiguous United States)
Orders with a merchandise subtotal of $500 or more (before tax) ship free by standard ground.
Orders under $500: flat $25 standard ground shipping charge per order.
Alaska and Hawaii: a $45 surcharge applies to all orders, in addition to the charges above.
Oversize items (marked 'LTL' on the product page) ship by freight and are quoted separately.

2. Dispatch
Orders placed by 2:00 pm Central Time on a business day ship the same business day. Orders placed after 2:00 pm CT, or on weekends or US federal holidays, ship the next business day.

3. Transit times (after dispatch)
Standard ground: 3-5 business days.
Expedited (2-day): 2 business days, $35 per order.
Overnight: next business day, $70 per order.
Transit times are estimates and are not guaranteed, except for Overnight, where shipping charges are refunded if delivery is late due to our carrier.

4. Damage and shortages
Inspect deliveries on arrival. Report visible damage or shortages within 5 business days of delivery through the customer portal, with photographs of the packaging and items. Note any visible damage on the carrier's delivery receipt when signing.

5. Title and risk
Title and risk of loss pass to the customer on delivery.

6. International orders
International shipments are sent DAP (Incoterms 2020). Duties, taxes and customs brokerage are the customer's responsibility.

7. Returns
See our Returns Policy. Restocking fees may apply.
response: Shipping is $25 (the order is under the $500 free-shipping threshold). It ships Friday because you missed the 2:00 pm cut-off, so with 3-5 business days in transit, expect it between Wednesday and Friday of next week.

question: I ordered $1,200 worth of lamps and decor from Lumiere & Oak, shipped by parcel carrier. Do I need to be home for delivery, and what happens if I miss it?
documents:
Lumiere & Oak Furniture - Delivery Information for Online Orders

Delivery options
Small items (lamps, cushions, decor): shipped by parcel carrier, 2-4 business days, $9.95 or free on orders over $150.
Large items (sofas, tables, beds): delivered by our two-person team, 5-10 business days, $129 per order, including placement in the room of your choice and removal of packaging.

Signature on delivery
Parcel orders with a total value over $1,000 require a signature on delivery from an adult aged 18 or over. The 'safe place' and 'leave with neighbour' options are not available for these orders. Orders of $1,000 or less may be left in a safe place you nominate at checkout.

Missed deliveries (parcel carrier)
If no one is available to sign, the carrier will leave a card and make a second attempt on the next business day. After two unsuccessful attempts, the parcel is taken to the carrier's local depot and held for 7 calendar days for collection with photo ID. Parcels not collected within 7 days are returned to us.

Returned-to-sender parcels
When an undelivered parcel is returned to us, we refund the order value to your original payment method within 5 business days of receiving it, less the original shipping charge. If you'd prefer to have it re-sent, a new shipping charge applies.

Large-item deliveries
We will contact you to book a 4-hour delivery window. If you are not home during the booked window, a $79 redelivery fee applies.

Damage
Please check items on delivery and report any damage within 48 hours via your account, with photos.
response: Yes, because the order is over $1,000, an adult aged 18 or over has to sign for it, and the safe place and neighbour options aren't available. If you miss it, the carrier leaves a card and tries again the next business day; after two failed attempts the parcel goes to the carrier's local depot, where you can collect it with photo ID within 7 calendar days. If it isn't collected, it's returned and you're refunded the order value minus the original shipping charge.
